gaps: The graph node unit.confined runs the declared confined suites serially and is not marked wall_clock: it holds its claim for about 1,900 s and would keep the ceiling on for most of the stage. Left to a later spec.
Bounds inside product modules and suite helpers under scripts/suites/support are named in a suite's notes where its rows depend on one; they were not surveyed line by line.
The decision does not ask whether CPU shortage can fail the row. Some declared windows are timers that must fire and cannot fail that way; their notes say so.
The spec's cost estimate covers the seven named suites. The survey declares 61, so the time under the ceiling is larger; the replay's admission record measures it.
deciding.method: Each part was read by hand from the scan hints in its chunk plus a search of the suite file for sleeps, clocks, timeouts, deadlines and waits. Parts 1, 2 and 4 to 8 come from the first build run. Part 3 was read again in the continuing build session, in the session itself; the first run's part 3 was set aside unread and is not an input.
deciding.rule: declared when the suite file holds a readiness wait, a deadline or a window under 30 s, or the spec names the suite; a hang guard alone declares nothing
